skill.name: convex-backup
skill.description: Export Convex snapshots and test recovery in a disposable preview or fresh personal development deployment. Plan a backup schedule, retention window, and production recovery runbook.
skill.summary: Back up Convex data and verify recovery in a separate deployment.
skill.author: convex

security_audit.summary: All seven backtick alerts are false positives for Ruby or shell substitution; the backticks mark Markdown examples and identifiers. The restore drill copies sensitive snapshot data into nonproduction without requiring equivalent access controls or approval for that data transfer. No evidence found of prompt injection or transfer to an unrelated destination.

remediation.issue: Sensitive snapshots can be restored to nonproduction without an explicit data handling check.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval for the data and target, and verify isolation and restricted access before import. Use sanitized data when feasible, and set a cleanup deadline for the restored data and local snapshot copies.

content.user_title: Back Up Convex Data and Test Recovery
content.value_statement: A snapshot alone does not show whether you can recover your Convex data. Restore it in a separate deployment, check the recovered records, and plan a backup schedule.
actual_capabilities: Identify the source deployment and export a ZIP snapshot, with optional file storage.
Recommend an export schedule and retention window based on acceptable data loss.
Restore a snapshot to a disposable preview or a fresh personal development deployment.
Check critical table counts and sample records after import.
Report drill results and outline a production recovery runbook with a deployment safety check.
limitations: Scheduled exports are recommendations. You must configure CI or cron and provide durable storage.
The preview drill requires a Preview Deploy Key and a paid tier. A fresh personal development deployment is the fallback.
Table counts and record samples do not verify every record or application feature.
The drill does not restore production. Restoring an older snapshot to production can discard writes made after the snapshot.

use_cases.title: Create a Portable Backup
use_cases.description: Export a snapshot before application maintenance and include file storage if the application uses it.

use_cases.title: Rehearse Database Recovery
use_cases.description: Restore a snapshot in an approved isolated deployment and verify critical tables before an incident occurs.

use_cases.title: Plan Backup Frequency and Retention
use_cases.description: Use the team's data loss tolerance to select an export cadence and retention window for user-controlled storage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a First Backup
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify the Convex deployment to back up and tell me whether to include file storage. Do not run an export yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are preparing your first Convex backup.

prompt_templates.title: Set a Backup Cadence
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a schedule and retention window for Convex exports. We can tolerate up to six hours of data loss and have user-controlled storage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Your team has defined its recovery point objective.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Restore
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the approved source and isolated target before importing the snapshot. Check critical table counts and sample records, then report the result without exposing record contents.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a snapshot and an approved nonproduction target.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Recovery Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the drill results to draft a production recovery runbook. Include deployment verification and the risk of losing writes made after the snapshot. Do not run a production import.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are preparing incident procedures after a restore drill.

output_examples.input: Verify our staging snapshot in the approved restore preview.
output: Drill passed in the approved preview. The Orders table matched the source count of 240, and sampled records matched the expected values.

output_examples.input: Report the drill result and recommend a schedule. We can tolerate six hours of data loss.
output: Drill failed. The restored Orders table contained zero rows, but the source contained 240.
Recommend exports every four hours to restricted storage. Confirm the retention window with the data owner.

best_practices: Confirm the source and target are different, and approve the data and access controls before restoring into nonproduction.
Compare critical table counts and representative records against the source, and report missing verification clearly.
Keep retained snapshots in restricted, user-controlled storage and delete temporary local copies after the drill.
anti_patterns: Use production or a shared development deployment as the drill target.
Treat a successful import message as proof that critical data was recovered.
Commit snapshots or include sensitive record contents in drill reports.

faq.question: Can a snapshot include stored files?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes an optional export flag for applications that use Convex file storage.

faq.question: Where does the restore drill run?
faq.answer: It runs in a disposable preview or a fresh personal development deployment, never in production.

faq.question: What if I do not have a Preview Deploy Key?
faq.answer: Use a fresh personal development deployment only after confirming that it is approved for the data. Report that you used the fallback.

faq.question: How does the skill decide whether a drill passed?
faq.answer: It checks critical table counts and samples restored records. An empty restore does not count as a successful drill.

faq.question: Does the skill install a recurring backup job?
faq.answer: No. It recommends an export schedule and retention window. You configure scheduling and storage separately.

faq.question: Does the workflow run a production restore?
faq.answer: No. It documents a gated production recovery procedure and warns that a restore can discard writes made after the snapshot.
